summary: A manufacturer of motorcycles, three-wheelers and Chetak electric scooters, with domestic, export and group-brand activities.
description: Bajaj Auto develops, manufactures and supplies vehicles for personal mobility and commercial use. Motorcycles, electric scooters and passenger or goods three-wheelers serve different customers; overseas demand is another important part of the business.
money: Revenue is generated by vehicle, parts and related business sales. Product mix, units, exports, materials, currency, distribution and investments in electric mobility and group operations affect earnings.
customers: Riders, commercial operators, dealers and export partners. A dealer’s purchase from the manufacturer can precede the final customer’s purchase.
drivers: Motorcycle and commercial-vehicle demand, export markets, model mix, electric-vehicle economics, materials and changing group boundaries.

groups.title: Motorcycles
groups.examples: Pulsar, Dominar, Avenger and commuter offerings.
groups.explanation: Price, engine category, performance and operating cost influence different riders and can produce different economics.

groups.title: Electric mobility
groups.examples: Chetak scooters and electric commercial vehicles.
groups.explanation: Battery sourcing, service capability, charging use and warranty costs matter alongside showroom demand.

groups.title: Commercial vehicles
groups.examples: Passenger and goods three-wheelers, including RE and Maxima offerings.
groups.explanation: For a working driver, financing, utilisation, fuel choice, maintenance and earning potential influence the purchase.

groups.title: Exports and associated brands
groups.examples: Overseas vehicle sales and activities involving KTM and Triumph under their respective group or commercial arrangements.
groups.explanation: Brand relationships are not interchangeable. Manufacturing partnerships and control of a company have different implications.

basics.title: Personal transport and a work vehicle are different purchases
basics.text: A motorcycle can be bought for commuting or leisure; a commercial operator assesses how a vehicle supports income. Their demand cycles and financing needs may differ.

steps.title: Design and source
steps.text: Develop vehicles and arrange engines, components, batteries and suppliers appropriate to the product.

steps.title: Manufacture to specification
steps.text: Use factory capability, quality control and production planning to supply the intended market.

steps.title: Distribute domestically or export
steps.text: Dealers and overseas partners manage availability and parts/service access.

steps.title: Support and reinvest
steps.text: Realised sales must cover production, marketing, warranty, development and the needs of newer businesses.

specifics.title: Exports are not one uniform market
specifics.text: Foreign exchange availability, import restrictions, local financing and political conditions can change dealer orders in individual countries.

specifics.title: EV growth needs a cost explanation
specifics.text: A scooter’s sales growth must be assessed with battery and component costs, service, warranty, pricing and any policy support.

specifics.title: KTM changed the group boundary
specifics.text: The FY 2025–26 chairman’s letter describes obtaining control in November 2025 and work on the Austrian business turnaround. Consolidated comparisons need the acquisition date and consolidation treatment, not an assumption that the group stayed unchanged.

watch: Billing, dealer stocks and retail differ.
Read domestic category sales and retail commentary together, with export inventory and partner orders where disclosed. Do not treat dispatch growth as an identical increase in rider demand.
What mix of vehicles drives the result?
Premium motorcycles, scooters and work vehicles have different costs.
Read category and geography performance, pricing and materials. Higher unit prices can accompany more equipment, marketing or warranty spending; a price list does not disclose model margins.
A recovery in one country can hide weakness elsewhere.
Follow country-level demand, currency access and trade restrictions alongside export quantities. Compare the same currency and period and distinguish shipment timing from sustained consumption.
Do electric vehicles earn enough after support costs?
Volumes alone omit some ownership costs.
Read EV pricing, production, battery arrangements, service coverage and warranty provisions. Identify achieved profitability versus management targets and the scope of any reported measure.
What does the KTM control change require?
Acquisition and turnaround costs affect group comparisons.

Use the FY 2025–26 acquisition and consolidation notes to identify subsidiaries, the period included, funding and exceptional effects. Keep standalone Bajaj Auto results separate from the wider consolidated group.
risks: Weak consumer or operator income and tighter credit can defer purchases.
Market restrictions, currency shortages and logistics can interrupt overseas demand.
Pricing competition, batteries, warranty and evolving regulation can alter expected returns.
Restoring a troubled group operation can absorb cash and management effort without an immediate profit recovery.
context: A commercial vehicle is part of a customer’s livelihood

Reliable service, parts and running costs influence how much work a vehicle can do. For commercial demand, investigate operator economics and credit availability as well as the manufacturer’s launch calendar.
quiz: Can consolidated growth be compared without reading an acquisition note?
No. A business entering consolidation can add revenue and costs for only part of a year. The scope, funding and exceptional items must be understood first.
sources: Chairman’s letter: KTM and business context

financialNotes.title: Use matching consolidation periods
financialNotes.text: Financial values remain pending verification for this profile. When entering them, distinguish standalone and consolidated reporting, the post-control KTM period and exceptional or financing effects. Do not treat each familiar vehicle brand as a separate reported profit segment.
